subsystems.name: Sensing front-end
subsystems.role: detects the microvolt-scale voltage rhythms produced by the brain.

subsystems.name: Real-time signal processing
subsystems.role: filters artifacts and classifies the current brain state (e.g. deep sleep, focused attention).

subsystems.name: Stimulation stage
subsystems.role: delivers a small, controlled current to nudge cortical activity toward a target state.

subsystems.name: Mechanical housing
subsystems.role: keeps electrodes in stable contact through hair and comfortable for hours of wear.

subsystems.name: Power and connectivity
subsystems.role: runs for a full night or work session and streams data to a phone.

subsystems.name: Companion app
subsystems.role: lets the user set goals, view sleep and focus trends, and control stimulation.

buildSteps.title: Design the electrode array
buildSteps.detail: Choose scalp positions (e.g. frontal for focus, mastoid for reference) and dry electrode materials that work through hair without conductive gel.

buildSteps.title: Build the analog circuit
buildSteps.detail: Amplify microvolt EEG signals with low noise, and design a constant-current stimulator with strict hardware limits on current and charge.

buildSteps.title: Write firmware
buildSteps.detail: Implement sampling, digital filtering, and real-time state classification, then encode closed-loop rules that trigger stimulation only when a target state is detected.

buildSteps.title: Train the algorithms
buildSteps.detail: Use public and in-house sleep EEG datasets to detect slow-wave sleep and focus-related rhythms; validate against polysomnography or expert labels.

buildSteps.title: Prototype the headband
buildSteps.detail: Integrate electronics into a flexible housing, test comfort, and measure signal quality across different hair types and sleeping positions.

buildSteps.title: Validate safety and efficacy
buildSteps.detail: Bench-test current limits, then run small sham-controlled human studies to see whether stimulation improves sleep depth or focus scores.

buildSteps.title: Iterate and scale
buildSteps.detail: Refine fit, battery life, and app experience; pursue regulatory clearance if making medical claims about sleep or attention.

prerequisites.why: they exist in consumer headbands, but reliable signal through hair without gel remains a challenge.

prerequisites.tech: Automatic sleep staging from wearable EEG
prerequisites.why: algorithms can approximate sleep stages, but accuracy varies and is not yet equivalent to clinical polysomnography.
research devices and some consumer products exist, but effects on sleep and focus are small, variable, and debated.
basic electrical safety rules apply, but long-term effects of repeated stimulation in healthy users are not well established.

pathway.milestone: consumer EEG headbands track sleep and focus; separate neurostimulation devices are sold for mood or training
pathway.unlocks: cheap, widespread access to brain-state sensing and a growing user base.

pathway.milestone: closed-loop headbands that stimulate only when a target state is detected, with dry electrodes that work through hair
pathway.unlocks: personalised, just-in-time nudges rather than continuous stimulation.

pathway.milestone: large sham-controlled trials measuring objective sleep and attention outcomes
pathway.unlocks: evidence to separate real effects from placebo and to guide safe use.

pathway.milestone: integration with other wearables and possible medical clearance for insomnia or attention disorders
pathway.unlocks: clinical adoption and reimbursement, moving the device from gadget to therapy.
